appraisal_events.evidence: celle que j'avais aimée n'était plus, au bout d'un certain temps, qu'un pâle souvenir; ... il m'apportait avec l'oubli une suppression presque complète de la souffrance; ... ce n'était qu'une tendresse de seconde main.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's forgetting reduces Albertine from an intensely loved presence to a pale memory known only second-hand through a superseding 'self,' diminishing her emotional hold on him.

appraisal_events.evidence: Ma mère, du reste, l'aimait bien, la plaignait de son infortune — suite des fredaines de son père ruiné par la duchesse de X… — infortune qui la forçait à vivre presque toute l'année à Combray.
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Sazerat is framed as an object of affectionate pity: her father's ruin has confined her to a diminished, mostly provincial existence, and her own dinner guests are described as boring.

status_effects.explanation: Albertine's place in the narrator's emotional life is clearly diminished, as forgetting reduces her to a faint, second-hand memory rather than a living object of love.
Mme Sazerat's social standing is somewhat lowered by the narrated account of her family ruin and forced provincial confinement, tempered by the affection accompanying the pity.

ambiguities: Albertine's 'diminishment' here is an internal, psychological process of forgetting rather than a direct social evaluation by another character; applying the appraisal schema to this introspective passage is a non-standard extension, so confidence is kept moderate.
The 'duchesse de X…' who ruined Mme Sazerat's father is deliberately anonymized in the text and is not resolved to any reference-sheet entity.
